ruling.recommended_action: Refund $2.74 (Ryde voucher, NS-7) for the unexempted 1.94 km off-route segment on this RydeTAXI metered trip; record the RD-1 breach on the driver's file (no account flag — RD-6 threshold not met).
ruling.reasoning:
RD-1: the trace confirms one off-route segment, F3 (14:28–14:34, 3.07 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.12 km, +1.94 km, up to 786 m off the optimal route). Under RD-1 any unexplained deviation breaches the driver's shortest-and-most-direct obligation, so this segment must be tested against RD-3 / RD-4 / RD-5 [F3][RD-1].

Consent (RD-5): F3 shows the segment started at 14:28:45, while the driver's route ask naming Clementi Road is timestamped 14:30 [F8] and the rider's "Sure, no problem." 14:31 [F9]; the chat record is complete and every message timestamped [F10]. RD-5 requires the rider's agreement to be sent before the segment begins, so the only rider consent on record post-dates the start and cannot excuse the segment [F8][F9][F10][RD-5]. The driver's post-trip written claim that the rider "said sure" is a statement, not the rider's own message, and G11 excludes a consent resting only on it — in any event F11 says no more than F9 already does [F11][RD-5].

Scope (RD-5 / G13): even disregarding timing, the agreement the rider gave was to a named road, Clementi Road, and RD-5 requires a record tying the driven segment to that road — a stop on it, a positioning message, or a road-name fact. Nothing in the record places the car on Clementi Road: no stop fact, no positioning message, and the only road names in the record are the congestion bands (Ayer Rajah Expressway, Jurong Town Hall Road, Kent Ridge Road) [F8][F9][F10][F12][F13][F14][RD-5]. Nothing places the segment elsewhere either — the driver's statement names no road for the driven path [F11] — so on the scope question the segment is named_road_untied and would be undetermined [F3][F8][F9][RD-5]. The timing ground alone already settles it as counts, and the two grounds are cumulative; the amount does not change either way, so the ruling can be issued on the timing ground [F3][F9][RD-5].

Reasonable cause (RD-4): the trace fails RD-4(a) — no incident on the replaced stretch reported before the detour — and F15 records no traffic incidents near the route during the trip window [F15][RD-4]. The only congestion record is a speed-band fact, AYER RAJAH EXPRESSWAY band 2 (10–19 km/h) 14:10–14:28 [F12]; RD-4(b) makes a band fact corroborative only and, on the MVP reading, it cannot exempt a segment on its own [F12][RD-4]. The segment is therefore an unexempted off-route segment [F3][RD-1].

Amount (RD-2, non-metered branch does not apply — this is RydeTAXI): refund = Σ unexempted extra_km × this trip's per-km rate = distance_fare $14.95 ÷ distance_km 10.60 = $1.4104/km [F7]; 1.94 km × $1.4104/km = $2.7362 → $2.74 [F3][F7][RD-2]. The excess-distance line billed $3.06 (2.17 km × $1.4104/km) is not refunded in full: the 0.23 km difference between the billed 2.17 km and the segment's 1.94 km is corridor/matching mileage outside every segment, which RD-2 leaves out [F4][F3][RD-2]. The $0.11 waiting charge is 0.4 min of metered waiting time on a RydeTAXI trip and is chargeable under RD-3(c); it is not refunded [F5][RD-3]. No surcharge or toll item is disputed, so FARE-1/FARE-2 add nothing [F7].

Account action: RD-6 requires the case to be established AND route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1. The driver's profile shows 1 prior dispute in 90 days but 0 route disputes upheld [F18], and the trace marks RD-6 ✗, so no flag_account is added; the RD-1 breach is merely recorded [F18][RD-6]. The rider's profile (0 of 2 disputes upheld) is not used to decide anything [F17].

Safety screen (SAFE-1): I read every message, the driver's statement and the complaint. F8 is a route request, F9 is a plain agreement, F11 is a factual post-trip account, and the complaint is about billing and timing. No threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation appears anywhere [F8][F9][F10][F11][RD-1].

segment_findings.reason: The off-route segment ran 14:28–14:34 [F3], but the rider's only consent message, 'Sure, no problem.', is timestamped 14:31 [F9], answering the driver's 14:30 ask [F8] in a complete, fully timestamped record [F10]. RD-5 requires the rider's agreement to precede the segment start; here it came after, so no rider consent excuses the segment and its 1.94 km extra counts under RD-2 [F3][F9][RD-5].

rejected_claims.reason: RD-5 requires the rider's agreement to be sent before the off-route segment begins. F3 fixes the segment start at 14:28:45 while the rider's own message F9 is timestamped 14:31 (ask F8 at 14:30) in a complete chat record F10, so the consent is consent_after_or_none rather than route consent [F3][F8][F9][F10][RD-5].

Agreeing to a named road covers driving on that road only, and RD-5 requires a record tying the driven segment to it. No fact places the car on Clementi Road — no stop, no positioning message, no road-name fact for the driven path; the road names in the record are congestion bands on other roads [F8][F9][F10][F12][F13][F14][F11], and in any event the agreement post-dates the segment start F3 [F3][RD-5].

RD-4 requires a traffic incident on the replaced stretch of the optimal route reported before the detour; F15 records no traffic incidents near the route, and F12 is a speed-band fact which RD-4(b) makes corroborative only and cannot exempt a segment on its own [F12][F15][RD-4].

Profile facts never decide a case on their own. The driver's clean history [F18] cannot exempt a segment that fails RD-3, RD-4 and RD-5; it is relevant at most to RD-6, where the profile shows 0 route disputes upheld [F18][RD-6].

The premise that no unexempted segment exists fails: F3 is an off-route segment that fails RD-4 (no incident, F15) and RD-5 (consent at 14:31 after the 14:28 start), so RD-2 prices its 1.94 km extra at $2.74 [F3][F4][F15][RD-2][RD-5]. The metered waiting-time point on F5 is accepted and that $0.11 is not refunded [F5][RD-3].

RD-6 needs route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1; the driver's profile shows 1 dispute but 0 route disputes upheld, and the trace marks RD-6 ✗, so no flag_account attaches [F18][RD-6]. The rider's profile is not used to decide anything [F17].
